subject: maths
title: Measuring and Comparing
seo_title: Year 1 Measuring and Comparing Worksheets: Length, Mass and Capacity with Informal Units (Free, with Answers)
standard_text: Measure the length of shapes and objects using uniform informal units and recognise that units need to be placed end-to-end without gaps or overlaps
meta_desc: Free Year 1 maths worksheets on measuring and comparing, matched to the Australian Curriculum (AC9M1M01, AC9M1M02): longer, shorter and taller, measuring with cubes and paper clips with no gaps or overlaps, heavier and lighter on a balance, which holds more, and ordering three objects. 100 picture questions with an answer key.
key_big: Line up the ends. Lay units end to end: no gaps, no overlaps, all the same.
key_sub: Count the units from one end to the other and say the unit: “6 cubes long”. On a balance the heavier side goes down. A bigger thing is not always heavier.
body_html:
Longer, shorter and taller

Put two things side by side. Line up one end. Look at the other end. The one that sticks out is longer. The other is shorter. For things that stand up, we say taller and shorter.

Measure with units

Lay cubes along the object, end to end. Start right at one end. Stop at the other end. Count the cubes. That number is the length. Say the unit too: “6 cubes long”.

Three rules: no gaps, no overlaps and all the units the same.

Heavier and lighter

Put two things on a balance. The heavier side goes down. The lighter side goes up. If the sides are level, they weigh the same.

Holds more and holds less

Fill a jug with cups of water. Count the cups. A jug that takes more cups holds more.

Order three things

A straw is 10 cubes long. A key is 3 cubes long. A pencil is 7 cubes long. Order them from shortest to longest.

Find the smallest number first: 3, then 7, then 10.

Answer: key, pencil, straw

How many longer?

A pencil is 9 cubes long. A crayon is 5 cubes long. How many cubes longer is the pencil?

9 − 5 = 4. Or count on from 5: 6, 7, 8, 9. That is 4.

Answer: 4 cubes

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Not lining up the endsStart both objects at the same line
Starting the cubes past the endPut the first cube right at one end
Leaving gaps between cubesPush the cubes together so they touch
Letting units overlapLay each unit just after the last one
Mixing cubes and paper clipsUse one kind of unit all the way
Thinking bigger means heavierUse a balance: the side that goes down is heavier

faq.q: What measurement do Year 1 students learn in the Australian Curriculum?
faq.a: Year 1 students compare and order objects by length, mass and capacity (AC9M1M01). They measure lengths with informal units such as cubes and paper clips, placed end to end with no gaps or overlaps (AC9M1M02).

faq.q: What are informal units of measurement?
faq.a: Informal units are everyday objects of the same size used to measure, like cubes, paper clips, paddle pop sticks or cups. They help children see that length is how many equal units fit along an object, before they use rulers.

faq.q: Why do the units need to be the same size?
faq.a: If the units are different sizes, the count does not mean anything. That is why two people using their own hand spans can get different answers, while two people using the same cubes get the same answer.

faq.q: How can I practise measuring with my Year 1 child at home?
faq.a: Measure a book or shoe with Lego bricks or paper clips laid end to end, compare two cups by filling them, and ask which of two objects feels heavier, then check on a coat hanger balance.

items.q: Which is longer?
items.e: Both start at the same line. Look at the other end. The pencil goes further, so it is longer. The pencil is longer.

items.q: Which is longer?
items.e: Both start at the same line. Look at the other end. The straw goes further, so it is longer. The straw is longer.

items.q: Which is shorter?
items.e: Both start at the same line. Look at the other end. The pencil goes further, so it is longer. The nail is shorter.

items.q: Which is longer?
items.e: Both start at the same line. Look at the other end. The texta goes further, so it is longer. The texta is longer.

items.q: Which is longer?
items.e: Both start at the same line. Both end at the same place. They are the same length.

items.q: Which is shorter?
items.e: Both start at the same line. Look at the other end. The strip of paper goes further, so it is longer. The crayon is shorter.

items.q: Which is shorter?
items.e: Both start at the same line. Look at the other end. The ribbon goes further, so it is longer. The eraser is shorter.

items.q: Which is longer?
items.e: Both start at the same line. Look at the other end. The paddle pop stick goes further, so it is longer. The paddle pop stick is longer.

items.q: Which is shorter?
items.e: Both start at the same line. Look at the other end. The caterpillar goes further, so it is longer. The worm is shorter.

items.q: Which is taller?
items.e: Both stand on the same floor. Look at the tops. The pencil reaches higher, so it is taller. The pencil is taller.

items.q: Which is taller?
items.e: Both stand on the same floor. Look at the tops. The straw reaches higher, so it is taller. The straw is taller.

items.q: Which is shorter?
items.e: Both stand on the same floor. Look at the tops. The paddle pop stick reaches higher, so it is taller. The crayon is shorter.

items.q: Which is taller?
items.e: Both stand on the same floor. The tops are at the same height. They are the same height.

items.q: The ends are not lined up. Which is longer?
items.e: The crayon ends further along, but it starts later. Slide it back so the ends line up. Then the pencil sticks out past it. The pencil is longer.

items.q: The ends are not lined up. Which is longer?
items.e: The straw ends further along, but it starts later. Slide it back so the ends line up. Then the ribbon sticks out past it. The ribbon is longer.

items.q: The ends are not lined up. Which is longer?
items.e: The paddle pop stick ends further along, but it starts later. Slide it back so the ends line up. Then the texta sticks out past it. The texta is longer.

items.q: You want to find the longer pencil. What do you do first?
items.e: Put the pencils side by side. Line up one end. Then look at the other end. The one that sticks out is longer.

items.q: A rope is longer than a stick. Which is true?
items.e: The rope is longer than the stick. So the stick is shorter than the rope. It is the same fact said the other way.

items.q: Amelia and Aarav stand back to back. Amelia’s head is higher. Who is taller?
items.e: Their feet are on the same floor. The higher head belongs to the taller child. Amelia is taller.

items.q: Mei’s string is shorter than Kai’s string. Which is true?
items.e: If Mei’s string is shorter, then Kai’s string is longer. Kai’s is longer.

sets.title: Measure with cubes and paper clips

items.q: How many cubes long is the crayon?
items.e: Count the cubes from one end of the crayon to the other: 1, 2, 3, 4. It is 4 cubes long. Count the cubes, not the lines between them. Touch each one as you count.

items.q: Count the cubes. How long is the key?
items.e: Count the cubes from one end of the key to the other: 1, 2, 3. It is 3 cubes long. Count the cubes, not the lines between them. Touch each one as you count.

items.q: How many cubes long is the pencil?
items.e: Count the cubes from one end of the pencil to the other: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7. It is 7 cubes long. Count the cubes, not the lines between them. Touch each one as you count.

items.q: Count the paper clips. How long is the eraser?
items.e: Count the paper clips from one end of the eraser to the other: 1, 2. It is 2 paper clips long. Count the paper clips, not the lines between them. Touch each one as you count.

items.q: How many cubes long is the ribbon?
items.e: Count the cubes from one end of the ribbon to the other: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. It is 5 cubes long. Count the cubes, not the lines between them. Touch each one as you count.

items.q: You measure a crayon with cubes. What do you count?
c: all the cubes in the box
items.e: Lay cubes along the crayon from end to end. Count only the cubes under the crayon. That number is its length.

items.q: Count the paper clips. How long is the leaf?
items.e: Count the paper clips from one end of the leaf to the other: 1, 2, 3. It is 3 paper clips long. Count the paper clips, not the lines between them. Touch each one as you count.

items.q: How many cubes long is the straw?
items.e: Count the cubes from one end of the straw to the other: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9. It is 9 cubes long. Count the cubes, not the lines between them. Touch each one as you count.

items.q: Count the paper clips. How long is the texta?
items.e: Count the paper clips from one end of the texta to the other: 1, 2, 3, 4. It is 4 paper clips long. Count the paper clips, not the lines between them. Touch each one as you count.

items.q: Where should you put the first cube?
items.e: Put the first cube right at one end. Then lay the next cubes end to end until you reach the other end.

items.q: How many cubes long is the caterpillar?
items.e: Count the cubes from one end of the caterpillar to the other: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6. It is 6 cubes long. Count the cubes, not the lines between them. Touch each one as you count.

items.q: Count the paper clips. How long is the strip of paper?
items.e: Count the paper clips from one end of the strip of paper to the other: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. It is 5 paper clips long. Count the paper clips, not the lines between them. Touch each one as you count.

items.q: How many cubes long is the paddle pop stick?
items.e: Count the cubes from one end of the paddle pop stick to the other: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8. It is 8 cubes long. Count the cubes, not the lines between them. Touch each one as you count.

items.q: Count the paper clips. How long is the worm?
items.e: Count the paper clips from one end of the worm to the other: 1, 2, 3. It is 3 paper clips long. Count the paper clips, not the lines between them. Touch each one as you count.

items.q: Which is longer?
items.e: The pencil is 6 cubes long. The crayon is 4 cubes long. 6 is more than 4, so the pencil is longer.

items.q: Count only the cubes under the nail. How long is the nail?
items.e: Count the cubes from one end of the nail to the other: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. It is 5 cubes long. There are 8 cubes in the row, but only 5 are under the nail. Do not count the extra ones.

items.q: Count only the cubes under the worm. How long is the worm?
items.e: Count the cubes from one end of the worm to the other: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7. It is 7 cubes long. There are 10 cubes in the row, but only 7 are under the worm. Do not count the extra ones.

items.q: Count only the paper clips under the pencil. How long is the pencil?
items.e: Count the paper clips from one end of the pencil to the other: 1, 2, 3, 4. It is 4 paper clips long. There are 6 paper clips in the row, but only 4 are under the pencil. Do not count the extra ones.

items.q: Chloe lays 4 cubes along a crayon. How long is the crayon?
items.e: Chloe used cubes, so say the unit: the crayon is 4 cubes long. Just “4” does not tell us what was used.

items.q: Which is shorter?
items.e: The straw is 8 cubes long. The texta is 5 cubes long. 5 is less than 8, so the texta is shorter.

items.q: Is this the right way to measure the pencil?
items.e: Yes. The cubes start at one end of the pencil and go to the other end. They touch with no gaps. They are all the same. The pencil is 7 cubes long.

items.q: Is this the right way to measure the crayon?
items.e: No, there are gaps between the paper clips. The gaps are not counted, so the number is too small. Push the paper clips together so they touch.

items.q: Is this the right way to measure the ribbon?
items.e: No, the paper clips overlap. Some lie on top of others, so you count too many. Lay them end to end.

items.q: Is this the right way to measure the straw?
items.e: No, the start is wrong. The first cube does not start at the end of the straw. Line up the first one with the end of the straw.

items.q: Should the cubes touch when you measure?
items.e: Lay the cubes end to end. They must touch, with no gaps and no overlaps.

items.q: Is this the right way to measure the pencil?
items.e: No, the units are mixed. Some are cubes and some are paper clips. A paper clip is longer than a cube, so the count means nothing. Use only one kind of unit.

items.q: Is this the right way to measure the texta?
items.e: Yes. The paper clips start at one end of the texta and go to the other end. They touch with no gaps. They are all the same. The texta is 3 paper clips long.

items.q: Mia left gaps between the cubes. She counts 4 cubes. How long is the pencil really?
items.e: The gaps are part of the pencil too, but nobody counted them. So the pencil is more than 4 cubes long. Push the cubes together and count again.

items.q: Is this the right way to measure the straw?
items.e: No, there are gaps between the cubes. The gaps are not counted, so the number is too small. Push the cubes together so they touch.

items.q: Noah left gaps between the paper clips. He counts 6 paper clips. How long is the ribbon really?
items.e: The gaps are part of the ribbon too, but nobody counted them. So the ribbon is more than 6 paper clips long. Push the paper clips together and count again.

items.q: Can you use cubes and paper clips in the same row?
items.e: Cubes and paper clips are not the same length. To get a length that makes sense, use one kind of unit all the way along.

items.q: Is this the right way to measure the paddle pop stick?
items.e: No, the paper clips overlap. Some lie on top of others, so you count too many. Lay them end to end.

items.q: Harper let the paper clips overlap. She counts 9 paper clips. How long is the texta really?
items.e: The paper clips lie on top of each other, so some length is counted twice. The texta is fewer than 9 paper clips long. Lay them end to end and count again.

items.q: Is this the right way to measure the strip of paper?
items.e: No, the start is wrong. The first cube does not start at the end of the strip of paper. Line up the first one with the end of the strip of paper.

items.q: Ethan let the paper clips overlap. He counts 5 paper clips. How long is the crayon really?
items.e: The paper clips lie on top of each other, so some length is counted twice. The crayon is fewer than 5 paper clips long. Lay them end to end and count again.

items.q: The crayon is 6 cubes long. How many paper clips long is it?
items.e: Look at the bottom row. Count the paper clips under the crayon: 1, 2, 3. It is 3 paper clips long. A paper clip is longer than a cube, so you need fewer.

items.q: Is this the right way to measure the ribbon?
items.e: No, the units are mixed. Some are cubes and some are paper clips. A paper clip is longer than a cube, so the count means nothing. Use only one kind of unit.

items.q: Leo measures a book with cubes. Zara measures it with paper clips. Who counts more?
items.e: A paper clip is longer than a cube. More cubes fit along the book. So Leo counts more.

items.q: The ribbon is 8 cubes long and 4 paper clips long. Why are the numbers different?
items.e: Both rows fit the ribbon exactly. A paper clip is longer than a cube, so fewer paper clips fit.

items.q: Cooper measures a desk with hand spans and gets 8. His teacher gets 6 on the same desk. Why?
items.e: A bigger hand covers more of the desk, so fewer hand spans fit. The teacher’s hand is bigger. That is why we use units that are all the same, like cubes.

items.q: Which is heavier?
items.e: The heavier side goes down. The book side is down, so the book is heavier.

items.q: Which is heavier?
items.e: The heavier side goes down. The watermelon side is down, so the watermelon is heavier.

items.q: Which is lighter?
items.e: The heavier side goes down and the lighter side goes up. The sponge side is up, so the sponge is lighter.

items.q: Which is lighter?
items.e: The heavier side goes down and the lighter side goes up. The egg side is up, so the egg is lighter.

items.q: The scale is level. Which is true?
items.e: The two sides are level. Neither side goes down. So they weigh the same.

items.q: Which is heavier?
items.e: The heavier side goes down. The stone side is down, so the stone is heavier. The beach ball looks bigger, but bigger is not always heavier.

items.q: Which is heavier?
items.e: The heavier side goes down. The tin of beans side is down, so the tin of beans is heavier. The pillow looks bigger, but bigger is not always heavier.

items.q: The scale is level. How many cubes balance the apple?
items.e: The scale is level, so the cubes weigh the same as the apple. Count the cubes: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6. 6 cubes balance the apple.

items.q: The scale is level. How many cubes balance the toy car?
items.e: The scale is level, so the cubes weigh the same as the toy car. Count the cubes: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9. 9 cubes balance the toy car.

items.q: Which is true?
c: The orange is lighter than 4 cubes.
The orange weighs the same as 4 cubes.
The orange is heavier than 4 cubes.
items.e: The orange side goes down. The side that goes down is heavier. So the orange is heavier than 4 cubes.

items.q: Which can hold more water?
items.e: A bucket is much bigger inside than a cup or a spoon. A bucket holds more.

items.q: Each container is full. Which one holds the most?
items.e: B is the widest and as tall as C. C is tall but very thin. So B holds the most. Tall does not always mean it holds more.

items.q: The glasses are the same size. Which has the most water?
items.e: The glasses are the same size, so look for the highest water. Glass B is nearly full. B has the most.

items.q: The glasses are the same size. Which has the least water?
items.e: Look for the lowest water. Glass C is nearly empty. It has less than D. So C has the least.

items.q: Each container is full. Which one holds the least?
items.e: C is the thinnest and the shortest. So C holds the least.

items.q: A bucket holds 8 cups of water. A bottle holds 3 cups. Which holds less?
items.e: 3 cups is less than 8 cups. So the bottle holds less.

items.q: Grace pours all the cups into the jug. Now the jug is full. How many cups does the jug hold?
items.e: Count the cups: 1, 2, 3, 4. The jug holds 4 cups of water. Do not count the jug.

items.q: William pours all the cups into the jug. Now the jug is full. How many cups does the jug hold?
items.e: Count the cups: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7. The jug holds 7 cups of water. Do not count the jug.

items.q: Ruby fills a bucket with a small cup. Oliver fills the same bucket with a big jug. Who pours more times?
items.e: A small cup holds less each time, so it takes more pours. Ruby pours more times.

items.q: You pour all the water from a tall thin glass into a wide bowl. Is there more water now?
items.e: The water looks lower in the wide bowl, but none was added or spilt. There is the same amount of water.

sets.title: Order three things and word problems

items.q: Which is the longest?
items.e: All three start at the same line. Look at where each one ends. The straw is the longest. The pencil is in the middle.

items.q: Which is the shortest?
items.e: All three start at the same line. Look at where each one ends. The eraser is the shortest. The crayon is in the middle.

items.q: Put them in order from shortest to longest.
items.e: Shortest first. The leaf ends first, then the texta, then the strip of paper. So: leaf, texta, strip of paper. Do not start with the longest.

items.q: Which is the tallest?
items.e: All three stand on the same floor. The straw reaches highest. The straw is the tallest. The pencil is in the middle.

items.q: Liam, Jack and Sienna stand back to back. Liam is taller than Jack. Jack is taller than Sienna. Who is the shortest?
items.e: From tallest to shortest: Liam, Jack, Sienna. Sienna is the shortest.

items.q: At the fruit shop, a pineapple is heavier than an apple. A watermelon is heavier than the pineapple. Which is the lightest?
items.e: From heaviest to lightest: watermelon, pineapple, apple. The apple is the lightest.

items.q: At the beach, Lachlan fills 3 buckets with cups of water. The red bucket holds 9 cups. The blue bucket holds 6 cups. The yellow bucket holds 11 cups. Which holds the least?
items.e: 6 is the smallest number. So the blue bucket holds the least. The yellow bucket holds the most.

items.q: Matilda measures 3 tables with paddle pop sticks. The red table is 12 sticks long. The blue table is 9. The green table is 15. Which table is the longest?
items.e: 15 is the biggest number. So the green table is the longest.

items.q: The book is heavier than the apple. The apple is heavier than the feather. Order them from heaviest to lightest.
items.e: The book is heavier than the apple, and the apple is heavier than the feather. Heaviest first: book, apple, feather.

items.q: How many cubes longer is the pencil than the crayon?
items.e: The pencil is 9 cubes long. The crayon is 5 cubes long. Take away the smaller number from the bigger one: 9 − 5 = 4. Or count on from 5 to 9: 6, 7, 8, 9. That is 4 more. Do not add: 9 + 5 = 14 is both together.

items.q: How many cubes shorter is the eraser than the straw?
items.e: The straw is 10 cubes long. The eraser is 3 cubes long. Take away the smaller number from the bigger one: 10 − 3 = 7. Do not add: 10 + 3 = 13 is both together.

items.q: At recess, Ava builds a tower 9 blocks tall. Isla’s tower is 4 blocks taller. How tall is Isla’s tower?
items.e: “4 blocks taller” means add 4. 9 + 4 = 13. It is taller, so the number must be bigger than 9.

items.q: A toy koala balances 7 cubes. A toy kangaroo balances 11 cubes. How many cubes heavier is the kangaroo?
items.e: Take away the smaller number from the bigger one: 11 − 7 = 4. Or count on from 7 to 11: 8, 9, 10, 11. That is 4 more. Do not add: 11 + 7 = 18 is both together.

items.q: A jug holds 8 cups of water. Charlotte pours 3 cups onto the school garden. How many cups are left in the jug?
items.e: Pouring out means take away. 8 − 3 = 5. There are 5 cups left.

items.q: Amelia needs 12 cubes to balance her lunch box. She has put 7 cubes on the scale. How many more cubes does she need?
items.e: Count on from 7 to 12: 8, 9, 10, 11, 12. That is 5. Or 12 − 7 = 5. Check: 7 + 5 = 12.

items.q: Aarav’s ribbon is 4 paddle pop sticks long. Mei’s ribbon is double that. How long is Mei’s ribbon?
items.e: Double means two lots of the same. 4 + 4 = 8. Mei’s ribbon is 8 paddle pop sticks long.

items.q: A straw is 10 cubes long. Kai cuts it in half. How long is each piece?
items.e: Half means 2 equal pieces. 5 + 5 = 10, so each piece is 5 cubes long. Double would be 20.

items.q: Chloe’s pencil case is 6 paper clips long. One paper clip is as long as 2 cubes. How many cubes long is the pencil case?
items.e: Each paper clip is 2 cubes. 6 paper clips is 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 12 cubes. Cubes are shorter, so you need more of them.

items.q: Mia measures the class mat and gets 9 hand spans. Noah measures the same mat and gets 7 hand spans. Who has the bigger hand?
items.e: A bigger hand covers more of the mat, so fewer hand spans fit. Noah got fewer, so Noah has the bigger hand.

items.q: A bottle holds 5 cups of water. A jug holds 7 cups. How many cups do they hold together?
items.e: Together means add. 5 + 7 = 12. They hold 12 cups. Do not take away: 7 − 5 = 2 is the difference.
